title: Make one tag one entry, however it was typed

blocks.text: The baking blog's tag cloud shows `crème` twice, with a different count under each, and a reader who searches for `jalapeño` from a tablet finds no posts although the cloud shows the tag. Both come from authors and readers on different devices. A food blog also has tags that really are different and only look alike, such as `rose` and `rosé`; those must stay apart.
`TagIndex` stores each tag under `key(tag)` and counts its posts. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/TagIndex.java`:

items: `key(...)`: the form a tag is stored and looked up in;
`postsTagged(...)`: the number of posts for a reader's search.

blocks.text: About two lines in total. The next practice builds a tag value class on the same idea.

cases.says: plain tags are counted per tag, and a search finds a tag's count, or 0 for an unknown tag
a tag whose accented letter arrives as one code point from one device and as a letter plus a combining mark from another is one entry
a tag with an accent and the same tag without it are two entries
a search typed in the other form of an accented letter finds the stored tag

origin.section: Text That Looks the Same Can Be Different Code Points: Normalize Before Comparing

concepts: The same text can arrive as different code points (é as U+00E9 or e + U+0301); equals and hashCode differ until both are normalized to one form such as NFC.
Removing accents is not normalizing: it merges different words such as René and Rene.
